descriptions: Compares flow dispersion (MAD) to peak flow levels to distinguish between stable expansion and erratic spikes.
Cross-sectional rank of the maximum net main fund flow over the window, identifying stocks with the most extreme institutional bursts relative to peers.
Peak flow normalized by volatility measures extreme expansion relative to recent flow stability.
Weights rolling information ratio of flow by the sign of its mean to capture risk-adjusted expansion direction.
Ranks the average recent flow across the cross-section to identify assets with relatively stronger flow expansion.
Computes the time-series correlation of cross-sectional ranks, assessing whether stocks with higher relative polarization magnitude coincide with higher relative net flow across the universe.
Measures correlation between the cross-sectional rank of normalized polarization intensity and the direction of net flow, isolating relative strength effects from absolute magnitude.
Computes the ratio of net flow weighted by the cross-sectional rank of imbalance magnitude to total flow, highlighting if extreme polarization stocks drive aggregate flow.
Calculates squared coefficient of variation to assess flow instability and expansion intensity relative to mean level.
Ranks the volatility range of large imbalances cross-sectionally to identify assets with exceptional flow expansion.
Risk-adjusted flow momentum using mean over standard deviation to normalize imbalance magnitude.
Ranks the volatility of money flow cross-sectionally to find stocks with unusually bursty flows.
Aggregates risk-adjusted flow performance with distribution shape for a composite expansion signal.
Ranks the maximum large imbalance level cross-sectionally to find assets hitting peak flow thresholds.
Normalized standard deviation measures flow volatility relative to average magnitude to detect unstable expansion.
Ranks stocks cross-sectionally based on the total number of days with positive net main fund flow in the last 10 days.
Peak flow intensity over the window normalized by average activity gauges maximum expansion pressure.
Standard deviation of imbalance normalized by recent peak magnitude to measure volatility stability during expansion.
Information ratio of imbalance series to measure risk-adjusted flow momentum and expansion consistency.
Calculates the skewness of the product of flow divergence and large buy share, detecting asymmetric behavior in sponsored divergence events.
Ranks the coefficient of variation of large imbalances to identify assets with high relative flow volatility.
Computes the information ratio of the product of retail and institutional flows to measure stability of their co-movement.
Normalized median absolute deviation measures robust volatility relative to average imbalance level to gauge expansion intensity.

This expression captures the single highest net main-fund flow over the past two weeks, which is useful for identifying recent, highly aggressive institutional accumulation events that set near-term support.
Calculates the rolling mean of directional agreement between retail and large sells to identify consistent panic sentiment.
Calculates the information ratio of retail imbalance to assess the consistency of retail signaling noise during market stress.
Normalized range measures volatility relative to average imbalance level to gauge expansion intensity.
Ranks the robust volatility (MAD) relative to mean flow cross-sectionally to identify outliers in expansion stability.
Calculates signed expansion intensity by weighting the range with the direction of mean imbalance, normalized by MAD.
Cross-sectional rank of medium-order imbalance volatility, identifying assets with unusually unstable shift patterns.
Rolling skewness of large buy shares, capturing asymmetry and directional consistency in institutional participation.
Computes normalized volatility of imbalances by dividing standard deviation by mean absolute level to gauge stability.
Cross-sectional rank of the number of days with positive fund flow in the last 20 days, identifying relative strength.
Averages the sign of imbalances over time to determine the net directional bias of large flow expansion.
Rolling information ratio of large flow imbalance, assessing risk-adjusted momentum of institutional flow changes.
Combines the direction of average imbalance with the information ratio to identify consistent directional flow expansion.
Scales the information ratio of large imbalance flows to emphasize risk-adjusted expansion intensity.
Correlates flow magnitude with signed flow to assess linearity of institutional participation.
Computes a robust normalized dispersion ratio using median absolute deviation, reducing sensitivity to outliers while gauging flow spread.
Time-series correlation between the magnitude of order imbalance and net main flow, assessing if larger polarization drives net directional flow.
